business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Canadian federal common law and Quebec civil law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), applicable to qualifying covered investments
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), applicable to qualifying investors
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), applicable to qualifying investors
Canada-China Income Tax Convention, where the investor or income source is Chinese
Canada-United States Income Tax Convention, where the investor or income source is United States-based
Canada-France Income Tax Convention, where the investor or income source is French
Canada-United Kingdom Income Tax Convention, where the investor or income source is United Kingdom-based
Other Canadian bilateral tax treaties and foreign investment instruments may apply according to the ultimate investor's residence and ownership chain

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal AML/CFT governance is principally under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. Quebec legal-entity transparency and beneficial-ownership filings are principally governed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, including the ultimate-beneficiary disclosure regime in force from 31 March 2023, and its implementing regulation. Canadian federal corporate beneficial-ownership rules under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, are relevant only where the entity is federally incorporated; a Quebec limited partnership is primarily governed by the Civil Code of Québec, CQLR, c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2230-2254, and Quebec enterprise-registration legislation. A wholesale used-machinery trader is generally not a reporting entity under the federal AML regime solely because it trades machinery; banks, payment institutions, securities dealers, accountants, lawyers and other regulated counterparties may nevertheless impose enhanced AML/KYC requirements.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all partners, directors, authorized signatories, UBOs, controlling persons, major customers, suppliers, banks, vessels, freight counterparties and beneficial owners against United Nations sanctions implemented in Canada, Canadian domestic sanctions under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code terrorist-entity list, FINTRAC guidance, and applicable foreign-risk lists including OFAC SDN and other relevant United States lists. Perform PEP, head-of-international-organization and family/close-associate screening using reliable independent sources. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for PEPs, sanctions-adjacent parties, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual wire transfers, cash transactions, third-party payments, circular trade and trade-finance activity. Apply ongoing monitoring, four-eyes approval for high-risk onboarding, transaction escalation, record retention and suspicious transaction reporting where a reporting entity is legally subject to the federal regime. Do not treat OFAC listings as independently binding Canadian law unless incorporated into the applicable transaction, contract, institution policy or sanctions-risk assessment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online enterprise register: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec limited partnership must use a name that complies with the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The name must not be confusing with an existing registered name, must not be misleading, and must not contain prohibited or reserved expressions without authorization. Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR, c. C-11, including amendments introduced by Law 96, the enterprise must have a French name and comply with French-language publication and public-facing requirements applicable to its activities. An additional English or transliterated version may be used only if legally compliant and properly declared. Latin-script transliteration does not replace the required French-language name where the Charter requires French compliance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Governmental, Crown, Royal, Federal, Provincial, Québec, Canada or municipal designations implying official status

Words or expressions implying a regulated profession, financial institution, bank, trust company, insurer, securities dealer, university, educational institution, charity or public authority without the required authorization
Names suggesting a connection with the government, a public body, an international organization or a protected institution
Obscene, discriminatory, deceptive or misleading terms
A name identical or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise name, trademark, trade name or protected designation
Words requiring sectoral consent or ministerial approval under applicable Quebec or federal legislation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Quebec generally does not provide a standalone statutory 30-day name-reservation period for a limited partnership equivalent to a reserved-name certificate in some other jurisdictions. Conduct an availability search and submit the partnership declaration or name-related filing promptly. If the Registraire des entreprises rejects or challenges the name, obtain the written reason, preserve the filing record, correct the name or provide supporting evidence of distinctiveness and authorization, and request administrative reconsideration through the Registraire's prescribed process. If the decision remains adverse, use the statutory review or appeal route available under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, including proceedings before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec where legally available and within the applicable deadline. A registered name does not create trademark rights; conduct separate CIPO trademark, domain-name and common-law conflict searches.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Quebec limited partnership must maintain a valid Quebec address and provide required information to the Registraire des entreprises. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable for registry purposes if it is a genuine service address, receives official correspondence, identifies the enterprise accurately and does not misrepresent business activity. It is not a substitute for operational substance where the partnership stores, inspects, repairs, finances, imports, exports or delivers heavy machinery. For used construction-excavator trading, maintain documented inventory controls, supplier and customer files, customs and shipping records, inspection or refurbishment arrangements, insurance, banking controls and personnel or independent operational capacity proportionate to activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official percentage is published. Baseline risk is low for a passive partnership with no regulated licence and no cash business, but practical inspection or verification risk is medium and may become high for cross-border machinery trading involving customs valuation, GST/HST or QST refunds, sanctions exposure, trade-finance instruments, high-value wire transfers, disputed inventory, tax audits or inconsistent registered-office information. Banks, Revenu Québec, the Canada Revenue Agency, the Canada Border Services Agency and other authorities may request documentary or physical verification without prior public notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2246 (société en commandite/limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 19, 23 and 28; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed with the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Québec law for a limited partnership; each limited partner must contribute as stipulated in the convention de société en commandite. Contributions in cash or in kind may be escrowed under the partnership agreement until the registration filing; non-resident limited partners are permitted, subject to disclosure in the declaration of registration and to Revenu Québec/CRS annual reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF THE CORPORATE GENERAL PARTNER OF THE QUÉBEC LIMITED PARTNERSHIP: (1) The limited partnership agreement is approved, and the capital contributions of the general and limited partners are accepted per Schedule A for deposit into the LP's Canadian bank account. (2) The registered office and principal establishment in Québec are fixed at the general partner's business address, with the Registraire des entreprises designated for service. (3) [Name] is appointed déclarant to sign and file the initial declaration of registration. (4) [Name] and [Name] are appointed managing partner and secretary, respectively, with authority to open bank accounts and execute ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary or independent legal counsel; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the convention de société en commandite in a notarial act if immovable property is contributed, otherwise in a private writing. Identify the general partner (commandité) with unlimited liability and the limited partners (commanditaires), fix capital contribution amounts and schedule, profit-sharing ratios, management powers, withdrawal rights, and bank account signing authority. Ensure the agreement complies with Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2246 and anticipates the publicity obligations of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Convention de société en commandite (limited partnership agreement)
KYC/AML dossiers for each partner (passport, proof of residence, source of funds)
Capital contribution schedule and proof of funding channels
Power of attorney of the general partner's representative, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any term is invalid or opposable under the Civil Code of Québec, rectify by a supplementary agreement or notarized correction deed prior to filing the declaration of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation with the Québec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online portal (clicSÉQUR / Registre des entreprises website)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Demande de réservation de nom electronically, including the legal designator 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C./L.P.'. Provide the proposed name of the partnership together with the reserved-name basis (distinctive element, descriptive element, legal designator). A name containing 'Québec' or a regulated expression requires an attestation from the competent body.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form
Identity proof of the general partner
Consent letter from professional order if the name implies regulated activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an administrative review before the same registrar within the stated delay and propose a corrected name eliminating prohibited grounds of refusal; the refusal notice contains the cure route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Initial Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – electronic filing through the Registre des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the reserved name file number, complete the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite. Attest the general partner's registered office in Québec, the principal establishment address (including the equipment storage yard or head office), the general partner's identity and legal form, and the capital structure. Pay the statutory fee; the enterprise number (NEQ) is issued upon processing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate/file number
Extract or summary of the partnership agreement
Identity and governing documents of the general partner
Address of the Québec registered office and principal establishment
Notarized power of attorney of the authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried or refused under sections 19 and 22 of the ALPED, file a corrected declaration or apply for rectification with supporting evidence; registrar decisions may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal of Québec (TAQ) within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Registration Certificate and Enterprise Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – immediate electronic certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificat d'immatriculation from the Registre des entreprises web portal as conclusive proof of the legal existence of the Québec limited partnership. Verify all registered particulars against the executed partnership agreement and the reserved name; retain the NEQ for subsequent tax and banking procedures.
required_dossiers: Certificat d'immatriculation issued by the registrar
Printed or PDF copy of the declaration summary for internal records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Obtain a certification or correction notice from the registrar to cure any minor variance between the declaration and the partnership agreement or to amend a registered address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online portal; Revenu Québec for QST purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a federal Business Number (BN) program account with the CRA through Business Registration Online. Using the NEQ and partnership agreement, apply for GST/HST program account, identify the general partner as the fiscal representative, and elect the partnership's fiscal year. In Québec, follow up with Revenu Québec to complete QST registration and to obtain tax installments accounts if employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Certificat d'immatriculation and NEQ
Partnership agreement listing general and limited partners
Tax residence certificates of non-resident partners, if applicable
Federal BN confirmation or CRA submission reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec requests clarification on partnership information returns, respond through the respective business portals and file a revised registration form; missing declarations can be amended online without penalty in most cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City/borough permits office (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Comptoir des permis) and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm with the local municipality whether a commerce permit or yard/storage permit is required for a wholesale dealer of used construction excavators under the applicable zoning by-law. Obtain fire safety clearance for any warehouse, shed, or fuel-storage area; complete CNESST registration for any employees and provide workplace health and safety training if operators or mechanics are engaged. No provincial industrial permit applies to pure wholesale remarketing of used earthmovers.
required_dossiers: Municipal commerce permit application and zoning plan
Evidence of lease or ownership of the storage yard and head office
Fire safety inspection report for enclosed structures
CNESST workplace registrations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a permit is refused, submit a revised operating plan restricting activity to wholesale resale with no on-site repair or fluid maintenance, or appeal the municipal decision to the municipal council or to the Administrative Tribunal of Québec as provided by local by-law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No standing industrial licensing authority for wholesale remarketing of used construction equipment in Québec; municipal commerce permits and CNESST workplace registration constitute the only physical licensing interfaces.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating licence is required for ISIC 4659 trade in used excavators; an optional municipal commerce permit (permis de commerce) and a yard utilization permit may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Québec; Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) for interprovincial hazardous waste movement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Triggered – pure wholesale resale of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers does not require a full EIA report or attestation. If the partnership later adds a repair, degreasing, painting, or effluent-producing washing facility, a section 22 environmental authorization under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, would then be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated in a pure trading model. For incidental storage, Québec's atmospheric quality and industrial effluent standards (CQLR c. Q-2 and its regulations) cap visible dust, require containment of hydraulic fluids, mandate leak-proof storage of waste oils, and prohibit soil contamination by uncontrolled spills; any future regulated wet-cleaning operation must meet REII/REAFIE-equivalent effluent thresholds and hazardous waste manifest requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire safety service for office, warehouse, and any heated storage shed; structural load inspection for loading bays capable of supporting crawler excavators in excess of 20 tonnes; CNESST occupational health and safety registration and operator training under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1) for forklift, crane, and excavator movement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal; Revenu Québec – ClicSÉUR Affaires portal for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial employer/agent registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Limited Partnership (LP) formed outside Canada but carrying on business in Quebec must obtain a federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) with an RC (GST/HST) account by filing the RC1 through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO). The LP is treated as a 'person' for GST/HST purposes (Excise Tax Act s. 240(1)) if it carries on a commercial activity in Canada. Step 2: the LP must register separately with Revenu Québec for QST under the Quebec Taxation Act using form LM-101-V or via ClicSÉUR Affaires. Step 3: if the LP has no physical establishment in Canada, it should appoint a representative for service of process using CRA Form RC59 and Revenu Québec Form LM-107-V. Step 4: the LP must open a CRA customs account (RM) for export/import reporting and maintain a T5013 partnership information return process for partner allocations. Step 5: each foreign partner's identity, residency, and participation percentage must be documented, as the LP is fiscally transparent and non-resident partners become subject to Canadian income tax reporting and potential Part XIII or Part XIV withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The LP is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax (income and losses flow through to partners) but is an independent registrant for GST/HST/QST when it conducts commercial activity. Available elections include: (i) a non-calendar partnership fiscal year-end election under ITA s. 249.1(4) where all members are non-residents or where a natural business period applies; (ii) GST/HST annual or quarterly filing elections and the quick method option for small suppliers under ETA s. 227(3); (iii) commensurate QST elections under the Quebec Tax Administration Act; and (iv) the election to limit partnership joint and several liability for GST/HST under ETA s. 272.1. No US-style check-the-box classification or blanket hybrid mismatch election is available under Canadian law; hybrid mismatch consequences are instead applied automatically under ITA ss. 18.4-18.9.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5% calculated on the GST-exclusive price; combined headline rate of 14.5% for taxable supplies made in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (GST/HST and QST) of worldwide taxable supplies for resident small suppliers; however, a non-resident limited partnership that carries on business in Canada is mandatorily registrable under ETA s. 240(1) and the Quebec QST regime regardless of the C$30,000 threshold where it makes taxable supplies in Canada. Registration is performed in the LP's own name and requires a Canadian business address or a designated representative.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API tax-authority clearance, or digital stamping for GST/HST/QST. Suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed information (ETA s. 221(1); QTA s. 434), including the seller's registration number, the date of supply, the total consideration, and the amount of tax. Electronic invoices are permitted where integrity and reliability of the audit trail are maintained. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework (Peppol PINT model) is voluntary as of the knowledge cutoff date. Books and records must be kept in Canada unless CRA or Revenu Québec has authorized retention outside Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% GST and QST rate may be claimed on the sale of used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers when: (i) the supply is made by the LP to a non-resident purchaser who is not registered under Part IX ETA; (ii) the heavy machinery is delivered or shipped by the LP (or at the LP's risk) for direct export from Canada; (iii) the goods are exported as soon as is reasonably practicable after the sale; and (iv) the LP retains contemporaneous commercial, customs, and banking evidence sufficient to demonstrate that the goods physically left Canada and that title passed to the foreign buyer. Sales structured as buyer's-own-export under a foreign purchase order and delivery to a Canadian carrier or customs-bonded warehouse are equally zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V s. 1 ETA and corresponding QST provisions. Quoted export transactions must also respect CBSA export reporting under the Customs Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form A6/CAED electronic filing) evidencing the HS code and declared value of the used excavator
Detailed commercial invoice with make, model, serial number, hour meter reading, year of manufacture, and sale price in CAD
Ocean or air Bill of Lading (or highway waybill) naming the non-resident consignee and destination
Outbound carrier cargo report or customs broker house manifest proving physical exit from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 payment instruction evidencing foreign-source settlement of the invoice
Title and acquisition records (purchase invoice, prior import documentation) establishing the LP's cost base and chain of ownership
Proof of delivery to the carrier at a port of exit, border crossing, or bonded warehouse
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess an improperly zero-rated export within the normal 4-year reassessment window, extended to 10 years where misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect is demonstrated. If export substantiation is deficient, the sale is recharacterized as taxable in Quebec, resulting in 5% GST and 9.5% QST becoming payable, with compound interest. ETA s. 280(1) imposes a gross-negligence penalty equal to the greater of C$100 and 25% of the net tax that would have been payable had the false statement not been made; egregious cases may trigger criminal prosecution under ETA ss. 327-335, exposing the LP and responsible partners to fines up to C$500,000 and imprisonment for up to five years, with parallel offence provisions under Quebec's Tax Administration Act. Partners of an LP may be jointly and severally liable for GST/HST/QST debts under ETA s. 272.1 and applicable Quebec law. Although Canadian federal law imposes no general statutory deadline for foreign-exchange repatriation in connection with zero-rating, CRA audits of cross-border heavy equipment traders require demonstrable evidence that export proceeds were received from outside Canada; failure to repatriate within the 180-day commercial benchmark may increase the risk that a purported export is recharacterized as a domestic taxable sale with full clawback of input tax credits previously claimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential and payments oversight by OSFI, anti-money-laundering compliance by FINTRAC, and cross-border transaction reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and the Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a fully convertible floating currency. Canada maintains no general foreign exchange control legislation; both current-account and capital-account transactions are substantially liberalized for non-resident persons and partnerships. Profit and capital remittances are not subject to exchange-control approval, but outbound distributions to non-resident limited partners are subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, normally up to 25% or a reduced treaty rate where an applicable tax treaty applies. Payment flows are also subject to FINTRAC large-transaction reporting and sanctions screening, but there are no convertibility, surrender, or Central Bank pre-approval rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory requirement to surrender, mandatorily convert, or repatriate export proceeds within a fixed timeframe. Used heavy machinery exporters may lawfully hold foreign currency in offshore or domestic foreign-currency accounts. The only material statutory duties are: (a) FINTRAC reporting of all electronic funds transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more entering or leaving Canada within 24 hours of execution, including the purpose code; (b) CBSA reporting of physically transported currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more; and (c) maintaining underlying trade documentation (commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration) sufficient to evidence an export transaction for banking and tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for pure offshore digital EMI-only onboarding. Canadian payment service providers must be regulated by OSFI as banks, federal credit unions, or authorized foreign bank branches; pure digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business) can provide virtual IBANs and multi-currency corridors but are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in Canada and generally cannot independently clear CAD-denominated CAD-A debit obligations. In Quebec, an entity providing payment services on an ongoing basis must hold or operate under a license under the Payment Services Act (Quebec) administered by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Recommended structure is to use a Canadian Schedule I bank as the primary operating depository and an EMI only as an inbound/outbound collection vehicle, with funds passing through the Canadian bank within 48 hours.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of at least the general partner and one controlling principal is generally mandatory for a non-resident Quebec Limited Partnership at the opening appointment of a Schedule I bank or its Canadian branch. Remote opening is available only where an existing Canadian banking relationship or a video-call KYC process is accepted, and then usually requires: original English/French corporate documents certified by a Canadian notary, a completed Personal Information and Beneficial Ownership form, and a sworn declaration regarding the LP's 25%+ partners. Fully remote opening is rare for an unregulated used-machinery trading LP; branch-based interviews materially increase approval probability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure of the Limited Partnership and lack of a public registry of limited partners in Quebec.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Certified copy of the Declaration of Partnership filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (b) full schedule of limited and general partners with current percentage interests; (c) attested beneficial ownership register identifying all individuals holding 25% or more; (d) passport copies and proof of residential address for each 25%+ owner; (e) audited or internally verified financial statements of the LP; and (f) a Quebec counsel legal opinion confirming the LP's creation, capacity, and binding authority of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or unclear source of funds for inbound capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Bank reference letters from the remitting institution; (b) source-of-wealth statements for each contributing partner (employment, real estate disposition, previous equipment-trading contracts); (c) notarized capital contribution certificates; (d) sworn declarations of no proceeds of crime; and (e) FINTRAC-compliant transfer records with precise purpose codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Used heavy-machinery grey-market risk: suspicious title, serial number alteration, stolen equipment, or prior use in sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin or OEM serial-number verification; (b) independent appraiser report (e.g., Ritchie Bros. Asset Management or licensed Quebec heavy-equipment inspector) with machine photographs and control numbers; (c) police/RCMP stolen-equipment database search report (e.g., Canadian Police Information Centre or the Equipment Register); (d) original bill of sale from a registered dealer/supplier; (e) customs export documentation from the prior jurisdiction; and (f) a written compliance attestation that the unit has never been operated in, or exported through, restrictive or sanctioned states.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical commercial substance in Canada and unstable projection for the LP's business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Quebec operating lease or warehouse/logistics agreement; (b) firm purchase or consignment agreement with a Canadian or third-country counterparty; (c) 24-month cash-flow forecast showing commercial turnover, not round-tripping; (d) correspondence with a Quebec chartered accountant and tax counsel confirming reporting obligations; (e) bios and resumes of the operations manager(s); and (f) reference to a confirmed end-buyer LOI or purchase contract for the first container/unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or trade-control concern due to international wiring to suppliers or buyers in unfamiliar countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Completed Canadian sanctions screening (CFSRA and United Nations Act) and OFAC/USD-cross-over checks; (b) end-user/consignee KYC forms for each foreign buyer; (c) contractual warranty that machinery will not be transferred to sanctioned persons; (d) use-before destinations and proposed export licenses if any controlled or military-grade commodities are involved; and (e) periodic positive confirmation of trade-finance compliance for each SWIFT beneficiary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for all capital injections from non-resident partners to the Canadian Schedule I bank account. The transfer should be routed to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account and carry: (i) beneficiary account number and bank BIC (e.g., BNDCCAMMINT for National Bank of Canada); (ii) obtain and quote a FINTRAC reporting reference if the transaction is CAD 10,000 or over; (iii) use the CPIS/G20 purpose code 'A500 - Direct Investment' or the Canadian purpose code 'Direct foreign investment in Canada' where required by the receiving institution; (iv) include a text line referencing the LP filing number (NEQ) and the capital contribution agreement; and (v) ensure the remitter's final beneficial owner is disclosed. No domestic conversion license is required; foreign currency may be received and later converted or held in a CAD foreign-exchange-linked operating account. The bank will run sanctions and CDD screening; funds are typically available T+1 after completion of the AML interview and the documented source-of-funds package.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlements for used excavator/roller purchases and cross-border sales should clear through: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers to pre-vetted supplier accounts, each transaction bearing an ordinary trade description, invoice number, and HS code 8429/8429.51/8429.52 where applicable, and using payee bank due-diligence matched to the underlying contract; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary MT700) for large-ticket units or first-time counterparties, with sight drafts against presentation of packed list, commercial invoice, original bill of lading, and independent pre-shipment inspection certificate; (c) SBLC or standby LC where a Canadian partner/consignor requires performance assurance; and (d) domestic/regional ETRs (electronic funds transfer through LVTS or Lynx) for within-Canada disbursements. Non-resident seller proceeds may be remitted abroad only after obtaining the appropriate FINTRAC record and satisfying the bank's compliance condition that the underlying equipment is lawfully imported/exported from Canada. All outbound USD or CAD wires must include the ISO currency code and, where applicable, the underlying customs export declaration number.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD interbank outright forward contracts (up to 12-24 months, executable with a Canadian Schedule I bank)
CAD/USD FX swaps for the conversion of export proceeds between transactions
Cross-currency swaps (CAD vs EUR, CAD vs CNY) where the Canadian bank can match the counterparty exposure
Vanilla currency options (USD call/CAD put or CAD call/USD put) for defined trade-account uncertainty
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only exceptionally for exotic or blocked currencies, not required for CAD as the CAD is fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) amending/confirming registration particulars of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the LP's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; applicable every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of 12% of the CAD 32 declaration fee; continued default triggers a formal notice, loss of legal publicity (inability to assert rights in Quebec courts), and administrative strike-off (radiation) after roughly two years of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return allocating income/loss to all partners (federal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following a calendar-year fiscal period; if a qualifying non-calendar fiscal period is used, the last day of the fifth month after fiscal period-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); increased penalties apply when partnership revenues exceed CAD 2,000,000 or after a CRA demand; partner deductions may be reassessed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return and RL-15 slips (Relevé 15) issued to each partner (provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quebec partnership information return due March 31 following the calendar year-end; RL-15 slips distributed to partners no later than February 28 and filed with Revenu Québec by February 28 (paper) or March 31 (electronic)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), plus per-slip penalties of CAD 100 for missing or defective RL-15 slips subject to statutory maximums; partner-level tax attributes may be reassessed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return and annual QST return (where the LP qualifies as an annual filer; otherwise quarterly or monthly remittances)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST) and Revenu Québec (QST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual GST/HST return and payment due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year LPs); annual QST return due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year LPs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GST/HST late-filing penalty of 5% of the net balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); daily compound interest on unpaid balances; QST late-filing penalty mirrors the federal rate structure under the Tax Administration Act; input tax credits may be denied until required information is filed

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a Quebec limited partnership solely because of revenue, assets, or partner count; an audit becomes compulsory when required by the partnership agreement, a unanimous declaration provision, lender covenants, or when an entity-partner is a reporting issuer subject to audited financial statements under National Instrument 51-102 or equivalent Quebec securities legislation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is the default framework for a private Quebec LP; IFRS (Part I) applies if the LP or any partner is a publicly accountable enterprise; financial statements must support T5013/RL-15 allocations and the annual declaration certifications required under Quebec's legal publicity regime

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises, due within 60 days of the registration anniversary, reconfirms the names, addresses, and roles of all general and limited partners; since the 31 March 2023 LPLE transparency reform, the declaration must also identify the natural persons who directly or indirectly control any corporate partner (beneficial-owner layer). A transfer or change in partnership interests must be reported as an interim amendment within 15 days and is not deferred to the next annual confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited partners, capital obligations, and share of profits)
Minute Book (decisions of the general partner, unanimous declarations, and consents)
Register of authorizations, powers of attorney, and corporate-agent appointments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per annum for a Quebec commercial registered-office or agent arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 for a contracted audit; USD 1,500 - 3,500 for a compilation engagement where no audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec corporate rate: 26.5% (15% federal + 11.5% provincial). For a Limited Partnership, income is allocated to partners and taxed at their respective marginal rates; the LP itself is not subject to corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific tax holidays for used machinery trading. General deductions include capital cost allowance (CCA) on depreciable assets, investment tax credits for eligible activities, and the small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporation partners (not at LP level).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) filed via CRA's EFILE; Quebec: TP-600 (Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes) filed via Revenu Québec's Netfile.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 due by March 31 for calendar-year partnerships (or 5 months after fiscal year-end); TP-600 due by June 15 for calendar-year partnerships (or 6 months after fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership identification: legal name, business number, fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Canadian business number (BN) and ensure non-resident partners are identified with their country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income or loss to each partner, including share percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners must report their share on their own Canadian tax return (if applicable).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of revenues and expenses, including gross sales, cost of goods sold, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all cross-border transactions are at arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance (CCA) schedule for depreciable assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply CCA rates per CRA class; non-resident partners must ensure consistency with their own tax filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for T5013: CAD 25 per day per partner, up to CAD 2,500 per partner. For TP-600: similar penalties under Quebec law, plus interest on unpaid amounts. Failure to file may also result in criminal prosecution for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Not applicable for LP distributions (pass-through). For corporate dividends, statutory rate is 25% (federal Part XIII) plus provincial surtax, but treaty relief may reduce to 5%–15% depending on jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners must file Form NR301 (or NR302/NR303 for specific income) with the CRA to claim treaty relief. Provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the partner's tax authority. For partnership income, non-resident partners must file a Canadian tax return (T1 or T2) and report their share of income, then claim treaty relief on the return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (Part XIII), treaty-reduced to 10% or 0% for many jurisdictions. Interest: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 15% or 0% for arm's length transactions. For LP, payments to non-resident partners for services or interest may be subject to Part XIII withholding if not properly structured.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for services; CAD 5 million for other transactions with non-residents. Documentation must include Local File, Master File, and Country-by-Country Report (if applicable).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like the UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. The CRA may recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance, especially for partnerships with non-resident partners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, inflating expenses, or failing to file T5013/TP-600.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Taxation Act (Quebec). Penalties up to 200% of tax evaded, plus fines up to CAD 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under the CRA's director liability provisions. For partnerships, general partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership debts, including tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation for cross-border transactions exceeding thresholds, or applying non-arm's length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments to income, penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (if documentation incomplete), and interest on reassessed amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the non-compliance. For LPs, general partners are personally liable for partnership obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, employees, or assets in Quebec, solely to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties for gross negligence. In severe cases, criminal charges for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may face personal liability for taxes and penalties if the entity is deemed a sham. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed under tax enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance (e.g., no KYC on non-resident partners, suspicious wire transfers without reporting).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 2 million for corporations and CAD 500,000 for individuals under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Criminal charges possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined or imprisoned if they knowingly fail to comply. For LPs, general partners are exposed.
